accuracy.evidence: Feature definitions follow Common Core RI.1.5/RI.2.5 wording (tables of contents, glossaries, bold print, indexes, headings) and the Year 2 programme of study on non-fiction structured in different ways: contents at the front in page order, index at the back in alphabetical order with page numbers, glossary for meanings of bold terms. Frog facts were checked: egg, tadpole, froglet, frog life cycle; adult frogs have no tail; frogs breathe partly through the skin and take in water through the skin rather than drinking.

misconceptions.evidence: Addresses the slips teachers report with search tools at this age: confusing contents with index (sort step and quiz tag glos), reading index numbers as chapters or counts (quiz tags chap and count, practice m2), scanning an index top-down instead of by first letter (look-up feedback names the starting letter and the ABC rule), and expecting the glossary to give pages (tool sort feedback). Mislabelling a time-order page as a list is caught by the build step and quiz tag list.

lab_distinct.evidence: flagnfind is a working mini book: a tappable contents page that opens the chapter's page number, an index where the learner must drop a new word into its alphabetical slot (the row position is checked against the ABC rule), a glossary matcher for the bold words on the page, and a page-structure identifier. flagbook labels covers and blurbs and flaglayout places writing devices; neither uses search tools, and the shingle gate passed.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child finds three chapters by matching words on the contents line and sees the page number to turn to, then experiences why ABC order matters by having to place legs between jump and pond. Matching bold words to glossary meanings, then sorting six real questions to the feature that answers them, makes the learner choose a tool rather than memorise definitions.

predictions.evidence: Three locked predictions with tempting wrong options: the contents page being at the back, index words being in the order they appear in the book, and looking up a bold word on the contents page. The front-of-book contents page, the alphabetical index the child then has to extend, and the glossary panel disprove each one in the same step, and the done message reports the prediction.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating challenge questions with twelve tagged wrong answers (glos, last, chap, count, cont, auth, abcf, abcs, list, qa, lastw, hmean), each explaining the particular confusion, e.g. that index numbers are page numbers, not how many ponds. In-lab feedback is specific too: a wrong index slot says which letters it should sit between, and a wrong chapter row quotes what that row is actually about.

readability.evidence: Kid explanation reads at FK grade 0.6 with short sentences and a worked example for each feature (What frogs eat … 10; pond 6, 7). Adult text is grade 7.2 and names the curriculum terms. Canvas text wraps onto two lines where needed at 360 px, and every label is a word or two.

no_filler.evidence: Every kid paragraph teaches one feature with a concrete example from the frog book; adult paragraphs give standards, terms, four named mistakes and a description of the lab. Items test using features (page arithmetic from a contents page, reading an index entry, ABC order, structure) rather than recalling the lesson's sentences.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots at 360 px Android light and dark and iPhone 13 light: the five contents rows and eight index rows fit on the page panel with page numbers right-aligned, the glossary sentence now wraps to two readable lines, the heading tag no longer overlaps the page heading, and the Question and answer tile wraps to two lines. Button twins wrap below the canvas and Show me completed all tasks on iPhone 13.

accessibility.evidence: axe-core found no WCAG 2.1 AA violations in light or dark theme on desktop and iPhone 13, with no console errors. Every row, slot, word and tile has a labelled button twin (including Put legs after jump), the canvas aria-label repeats each result, and correct and wrong states use a border and text message as well as colour.

sources: Common Core State Standards for English Language Arts: RI.1.5, RI.2.5, RI.3.5 (text features and search tools)

DfE (2013) English programmes of study: key stages 1 and 2, Year 2 reading comprehension (non-fiction books structured in different ways) and lower key stage 2 (retrieve and record information from non-fiction)
Natural History Museum / Froglife guidance on the common frog life cycle (spawn, tadpole, froglet, frog) and amphibian skin respiration and water uptake
